subject: Music Production
title: How Loud Is Too Loud
description: A quick, practical guide to How Loud Is Too Loud.

hook.text: A whisper measures about thirty decibels, while a rock concert blasts at over one hundred ten.

buildup.text: Prolonged exposure above eighty-five decibels begins to damage the delicate hair cells in the ear.

discovery.text: Once those hair cells are destroyed, they never regenerate, and the hearing loss is permanent.

twist.text: Many famous producers and musicians suffer hearing damage from years of loud studio monitoring.

climax.text: Modern producers wear custom ear protection and mix at moderate levels to preserve their ears.

punchline.text: The ears that make music can be destroyed by it.

quiz.question: At what decibel level does hearing damage begin?
